definition_zh: n. 大提琴
definition_en: a large string instrument with four strings, played with a bow and held between the knees
core_image: 低沉的琴声从木箱里铺开
scene: 她把大提琴夹在两膝之间，拉出一个低长的音。She held the cello between her knees and drew a long low note.

senses.title: The instrument
senses.definition: a large string instrument with four strings, played with a bow
senses.definitionCN: 四弦、用弓演奏的大型弦乐器
senses.example: The cello has a deep warm voice.

items.en: Violoncello names a smaller violone.

items.en: Players shorten the name to cello.

items.en: The cello takes its place in the orchestra.
items.cn: 十九世纪大提琴在管弦乐队中定型。

normal.en: Violone was a large viol.

normal.en: Violoncello means a small large viol.

normal.en: Players shortened it to cello.

definition_zh: 手机；移动电话；蜂窝电话
definition_en: a telephone that can be carried everywhere and works through a network of radio stations arranged in cells
core_image: 握在掌心的小窗：一块巴掌大的屏幕，把千里之外的人拉到耳边
scene: 地铁到站前，她把耳机塞进耳朵，低头看着屏幕上的未读消息轻轻微笑。She checks every message on her cellphone before the train reaches the station.
sceneCN: 这里 cellphone 是「手机、移动电话」（第 1 个义项：随身携带的通话设备）；句意是她在地铁到站前查看手机上的每一条未读消息。

pos.zh: 手机；移动电话；蜂窝电话

derivatives.zh: 同义表达，mobile 源自拉丁 mobilis（可移动的），义为「移动电话」
由 cell 加形容词后缀构成，义为「蜂窝状的；细胞的」
由希腊词根 tele-（远）+ phone（声音）构成，义为「电话」

senses.title: A portable telephone
senses.definition: a small telephone that you can carry with you and use anywhere
senses.definitionCN: 可以随身携带、在任何地方使用的电话设备
senses.example: She left her cellphone at home and felt cut off all day.
senses.exampleCN: 她把手机忘在家里，一整天都觉得与世隔绝。
senses.why: The word joins cell, the radio zones of the network, with phone, sound; the object is literally a phone served by cells.
senses.whyCN: cellphone 由 cell（网络中的蜂窝小区）与 phone（声音）合成，字面义就是「由蜂窝小区提供服务的电话」，核心义项由此而来。

senses.title: The device as a personal tool
senses.definition: the device regarded as someone's personal property and daily companion
senses.definitionCN: 被视为个人财物与日常伴侣的那部手机
senses.example: My cellphone holds my photos, notes and timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 我的手机里存着我的照片、笔记和课程表。
senses.why: Once everyone owns one phone, the word shifts from a kind of device to that one device a person carries.
senses.whyCN: 当人手一部手机时，词义从「一类设备」滑向「某人随身的那一部」，泛指义收缩为特定义。

senses.title: Phone calls made on it
senses.definition: a call or conversation made using a cellphone
senses.definitionCN: 用手机打出的电话或进行的通话
senses.example: The interview was arranged over a cellphone.
senses.exampleCN: 这次面试是用手机电话约定的。
senses.why: In English a device often stands for the activity done with it, so cellphone can mean the call itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语里常用工具名词转指用它做的事，cellphone 借这种转喻从设备转指「通话」这一行为结果。

senses.title: Mobile communication in general
senses.definition: the technology or system of wireless mobile communication
senses.definitionCN: 无线移动通信的技术或体系
senses.example: The valley has no cellphone coverage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷没有手机信号覆盖。
senses.why: Because the network, not just the handset, makes calls possible, the word also names the whole system.
senses.whyCN: 手机能通话依赖整张蜂窝网络，于是该词又扩展指「移动通信体系」，如信号、覆盖、制式。

senses.title: Used before another noun
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：手机的、手机用的
senses.definition: placed before a noun to show the noun belongs to the world of cellphones
senses.definitionCN: 置于另一名词前，表示该名词属于手机的范畴
senses.example: A cellphone camera cannot replace a studio lens.
senses.exampleCN: 手机摄像头无法取代影棚镜头。
senses.why: Nouns in English commonly modify other nouns directly, so cellphone easily becomes a classifier.
senses.whyCN: 英语名词可以直接修饰名词，cellphone 因此常用作限定语，派生出手机电池、手机号码等复合表达。

senses.title: British everyday word
senses.definition: the ordinary everyday word for a mobile phone in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 英国日常口语中对移动电话的普通叫法
senses.example: Switch your cellphone off in the cinema, please.
senses.exampleCN: 在影院里请把手机关掉。
senses.why: Different regions fixed on different names: Britain said cellphone, America preferred cell phone or cellular phone.
senses.whyCN: 各地对同一设备固定了不同叫法：英国常说 cellphone，美国多用 cell phone 或 cellular phone，形成地域变体。

senses.title: A symbol of constant contact
senses.definition: the idea of being always reachable, considered figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻意义上「随时可以被联系到」的状态
senses.example: The cellphone has erased the border between office and home.
senses.exampleCN: 手机抹去了办公室与家之间的界限。
senses.why: Because the device never leaves the owner, it becomes a ready symbol for endless reachability.
senses.whyCN: 由于手机从不离身，它自然成为「随时在线、无法断联」这种现代处境的象征。

senses.title: The object in rules and bans
senses.titleCN: 规章中的手机（禁用对象）
senses.definition: the device mentioned in rules about where it may or may not be used
senses.definitionCN: 在各类场所规章里被点名允许或禁止使用的设备
senses.example: Cellphones are banned in the examination hall.
senses.exampleCN: 考场内禁止使用手机。
senses.why: When a device becomes common enough to cause problems, institutions name it in their rules.
senses.whyCN: 当设备普及到需要管理时，规章便直接点名它，于是 cellphone 在禁令、条款类语境中高频出现。

intro.en: Cellphone is a modern compound, but both halves are old: cell from Latin cella, phone from Greek phōnē.
intro.cn: cellphone 是现代合成词，但两个成分都很古老：cell 来自拉丁语 cella，phone 来自希腊语 phōnē。

items.en: The root *(s)kel-, generally reconstructed, meant to bend or turn; it later fed words for small enclosed spaces.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *(s)kel- 义为「弯曲、转动」，后来衍生出表示「小隔间」的一族词。

items.en: Latin cella meant a small room or storeroom, such as a monk's cell; it also gave biological cell.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 指小房间、储藏室（如僧侣的小室），生物学里的「细胞」cell 亦出于此。

items.en: Greek phōnē meant voice or sound; it reached English through telephone, coined in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 希腊语 phōnē 义为「声音、嗓音」，经十九世纪新造的 telephone 进入英语的构词系统。

items.en: Engineers divided a coverage area into small zones called cells, each with its own transmitter; the network was called cellular.
items.cn: 工程师把覆盖区划分为多个小服务区，每个小区设一台发射机，这种网被称为「蜂窝网」cellular。

items.en: As handsets spread, cell phone and cellphone were clipped from cellular telephone and quickly became the everyday words.
items.cn: 随手持电话普及，cellular telephone 被截短为 cell phone / cellphone，迅速成为日常叫法。

items.en: British spelling settled on one word cellphone, while American writing often keeps the two-word cell phone.
items.cn: 英式拼写定型为合写的 cellphone，美式书面语则常保留分写的 cell phone。

note.en: Compare the members of the cell family and the near-synonyms for a hand-carried phone.
note.cn: 对比 cell 词族各成员，以及表示「手提电话」的近义说法。

entries.definition: of or made of small cells; in cellular phone, of a network divided into cells
entries.definitionCN: 蜂窝状的；细胞的；cellular phone 中的 cellular 指「蜂窝网的」

entries.definition: a device for transmitting voice over distance; the full form from which cellphone was clipped
entries.definitionCN: 电话；cellphone 截短所依据的完整旧词

entries.definition: a large bowed string instrument; only shares letters with cellphone, no relation in origin
entries.definitionCN: 大提琴；只是拼写开头相近，词源与 cellphone 无关

entries.definition: the standard British name for the same device
entries.definitionCN: 移动电话；英式英语对同一设备的标准称呼

entries.definition: a cellphone with computer-like functions such as apps and internet access
entries.definitionCN: 智能手机；带应用程序和上网功能的手机

entries.definition: the part of a phone held in the hand, or the whole phone in industry jargon
entries.definitionCN: 听筒；（行业用语里的）整部手机

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its two old parts and the network idea behind them.
normalIntro.cn: 从两个古老成分和背后的蜂窝网概念来搭建这个词。

normal.en: cell = Latin cella, a small room; each radio zone is one small room of the network.
normal.cn: cell 来自拉丁语 cella「小房间」，网络里每个服务区就是一间小房间。

normal.en: phone = Greek phōnē, voice; the same part appears in telephone and microphone.
normal.cn: phone 来自希腊语 phōnē「声音」，telephone、microphone 里都有它。

normal.en: cellular telephone is the long form; cellphone is the clipped everyday form.
normal.cn: cellular telephone 是完整说法，cellphone 是截短后的日常说法。

normal.en: Hexagon cells packed together look like honeycomb, hence cellular network.
normal.cn: 许多六边形小区拼在一起形似蜂巢，故称蜂窝网。

normal.en: cellphones = cell + phone + s, the plural simply adds the s.
normal.cn: 复数 cellphones 只需在词尾加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a city cut into honeycomb rooms, each with its own little transmitter.
abstract.cn: 把城市想象成被切成一间间蜂房，每间房里装着一个小发射器。

abstract.en: Imagine your phone as a bee hopping from cell to cell as you travel.
abstract.cn: 把手机想成一只蜜蜂，你移动时它在蜂房间不停跳转。

abstract.en: One word, one object in the palm: cell plus phone equals the phone that roams.
abstract.cn: 一词一物：cell 加 phone，就是那台会漫游的电话。

examples.en: Please switch your cellphone to silent during the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会期间请把手机调成静音。

examples.en: He lost his cellphone on the bus and lost all his contacts with it.
examples.cn: 他把手机丢在了公交车上，连同所有联系人一起丢了。

examples.en: Good signal makes every journey feel shorter.
examples.cn: 信号好的时候，每段旅程都显得更短。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛欧风」——手机像赛场吹过的风，走到哪儿跟到哪儿；cell（蜂窝小区）+ phone（声音），声音随蜂窝网四处流动。

root: cellphone 为复合词：cell 源自拉丁语 cella（小房间），在电信语境指蜂窝网络中的一个个服务小区；phone 源自希腊语 phōnē（声音），是 telephone、microphone 等词的共同成分。两截拼接即「由蜂窝小区网络承载的电话」。

sensesIntro.en: From the device itself, the meaning fans out to the person's own phone, the calls, the network, and its figurative weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 从设备本义出发，词义扩展到个人手机、通话、移动通信体系，再到规章与比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone served by honeycomb cells
core.cn: 核心意象：由一个个蜂窝小区托起、随人而行的电话

branches.en: From the generic device to the one phone a person owns
branches.cn: 由泛指设备到某人随身的那一部手机

branches.en: The device stands for the calls made on it
branches.cn: 设备转指用它进行的通话

branches.en: The network behind it and the compound uses it generates
branches.cn: 背后的移动通信体系及其派生的复合用法

branches.en: Regional naming habits fix the everyday word
branches.cn: 地域称呼习惯固化日常用语

branches.en: Figurative weight and its place in rules
branches.cn: 比喻意涵与规章中的禁用对象

intro.en: Cellphone is a plain compound, but its pieces carry Greek and Latin load-bearing parts reused across technical English.
intro.cn: cellphone 是朴素的复合词，但它的构件带有希腊、拉丁词根，在科技英语中被反复复用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin side of the family centers on cella, a small room, which also powers cellular and cell in biology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语一侧以 cella（小房间）为中心，它同时支撑着 cellular 与生物学里的 cell。

items.example: Each cell of the network has its own antenna.
items.exampleCN: 网络的每个小区都有自己的天线。

items.example: A cellular network covers a city zone by zone.
items.exampleCN: 蜂窝网按小区逐片覆盖城市。

items.example: The phone rang right after lunch.

items.exampleCN: telephone 字面义是「把声音送向远方」。

items.example: A microphone turns sound into a signal.
items.exampleCN: 麦克风把声音变成电信号。

items.meaning: the science of sounds of speech
items.example: Phonics teaching links letters to sounds.
items.exampleCN: 语音教学法把字母和读音对应起来。

items.example: The cellist tuned her strings backstage.
items.exampleCN: 大提琴手在后台给琴弦调音。
flour 和 flower 是同音词。

items.example: Wine sleeps best in a cool cellar.
items.exampleCN: 葡萄酒在阴凉的地窖里存放最好。

items.meaning: a wind instrument named after Sax
items.example: A saxophone led the street band.
items.exampleCN: 萨克斯管领着街头乐队。

latinEntries.example: The cella held the temple's statue.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 内室中供奉着神庙的雕像。

latinEntries.example: Each monk wrote in his cellula.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 每位僧侣在自己的小室里抄写。
该词描述蜂窝状的组织。

definition_zh: 细胞的；由细胞组成的；蜂窝式的
definition_en: relating to cells, made of cells, or organised in a honeycomb pattern
core_image: 一排小房间彼此相邻，每个房间里都有一套完整的生命装置
scene: 生物课上讲到细胞结构时，老师画了一个细胞。The new phone network divides the city into small cellular areas.
sceneCN: 这里 cellular 指「蜂窝式的」（第 4 个义项：把覆盖区分成许多小格来复用频率）；句意：新的电话网络把城市划分成许多蜂窝式小区。

pos.zh: 细胞的；由细胞组成的；蜂窝式的；（电信）蜂窝网络的

senses.title: Made of cells
senses.definition: consisting of or built from biological cells
senses.definitionCN: 由生物细胞构成或组成的
senses.example: Muscle is a cellular tissue with many nuclei per fibre.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉是一种多核的细胞组织。
senses.why: The adjective form of cell simply says that something is made of the units biology calls cells.
senses.whyCN: cell 的形容词形式最直接的意思就是：某物由生物学称为「细胞」的那些单元构成。

senses.title: Of cell biology
senses.titleCN: 细胞层面的；细胞生物学的
senses.definition: relating to the study or level of cells
senses.definitionCN: 与细胞研究或细胞层面有关的
senses.example: Cellular biology examines how organelles cooperate.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞生物学考察各种细胞器如何协作。
senses.why: Once cells are a level of organisation, the adjective labels the science and the scale that studies that level.
senses.whyCN: 一旦细胞成为一个组织层次，这个形容词就用来标记研究该层次的科学与尺度。

senses.title: Inside a cell
senses.definition: happening or located inside a cell
senses.definitionCN: 发生在细胞内或位于细胞内的
senses.example: Cellular responses to stress begin within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞对压力的反应在几分钟内就开始。
senses.why: A response that occurs inside the cell belongs to the cell, so the adjective shifts from composition to location and process.
senses.whyCN: 发生在细胞内部的反应属于细胞，于是这个形容词从「由什么构成」转向「在哪里发生」。

senses.title: Honeycomb network
senses.definition: describing a radio network that divides an area into small overlapping cells
senses.definitionCN: 指把一片区域划分为许多相互重叠的小区的无线电网络
senses.example: Cellular coverage in the valley improved after two new towers went up.
senses.exampleCN: 两座新塔建成后，山谷里的蜂窝网络覆盖改善了。
senses.why: Radio engineers borrowed the honeycomb image because each base station covers a small cell and neighbouring cells reuse frequencies.
senses.whyCN: 无线电工程师借用了蜂巢的意象，因为每个基站覆盖一个小格，相邻小格可以重复使用频率。

senses.title: Cellular phone
senses.definition: relating to a mobile telephone system that uses cellular cells
senses.definitionCN: 指使用蜂窝小区的移动电话系统
senses.example: He called from a cellular phone while crossing the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿越沙漠时用蜂窝电话打来。
senses.why: The phone is named after the network that makes it work, so cellular became an everyday word for mobile.
senses.whyCN: 这种电话因支撑它的网络而得名，因此 cellular 在日常英语里就成了「移动的」之意。

senses.title: Cell-mediated immunity
senses.definition: describing immunity carried out by living cells rather than by antibodies alone
senses.definitionCN: 指由活细胞而不是仅由抗体执行的免疫
senses.example: Cellular immunity keeps the virus from spreading between cells.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞免疫阻止病毒在细胞之间扩散。
senses.why: Immunology contrasts cell-based defence with antibody-based defence, and the adjective marks the cell side of that contrast.
senses.whyCN: 免疫学把以细胞为主的防御与以抗体为主的防御相对照，这个形容词标出对照中的细胞一侧。

senses.title: Porous structure
senses.definition: describing a material or structure full of small open compartments
senses.definitionCN: 指充满小空腔的材料或结构
senses.example: Cellular concrete is light because air fills its pores.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂窝混凝土很轻，因为空气填满了它的孔隙。
senses.why: The honeycomb image, once borrowed by engineers, also describes foams, concrete and packaging with many small cells.
senses.whyCN: 蜂巢意象一旦被工程师借用，也能描述泡沫、混凝土与包装材料里那许多小格。

senses.title: Cellular automaton
senses.definition: in computing, describing a grid of simple units whose states update by fixed rules
senses.definitionCN: 计算领域指由简单单元组成的网格，按固定规则更新状态
senses.example: The model is a cellular automaton that simulates traffic flow.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型是一个模拟交通流的元胞自动机。
senses.why: Each grid square acts like a tiny cell, so mathematicians reused the biological word for a lattice of rule-following units.
senses.whyCN: 每个网格方块像一个小细胞，因此数学家把生物学词汇借用来指一张按规则运行的格点。

senses.title: Solitary confinement
senses.definition: in penal history, describing confinement of one prisoner to one cell
senses.definitionCN: 刑罚史中指把一名囚犯单独关在一间牢房里
senses.example: The prison abolished cellular confinement for long sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 该监狱废除了对长期刑犯使用单人牢房的做法。
senses.why: The oldest sense of cell is a small room, and cellular keeps that history alive in the language of prisons.
senses.whyCN: cell 最古老的意义就是小房间，cellular 在监狱用语中保留了这段历史。

intro.en: Cellular is a Latin diminutive turned adjective: a small room becomes a biological unit, and then a honeycomb pattern in engineering.
intro.cn: cellular 是拉丁语指小词变来的形容词：小房间先变成生物学单元，再变成工程里的蜂窝结构。

items.en: Latin cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine. It is related to cellarium, a storehouse, and to the English words cellar and cell.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 指小房间、储藏室或神龛。它与 cellarium「仓库」同源，也衍生出英语 cellar 与 cell。

items.en: The diminutive cellula, 'little room', supplied the base for the adjective. The suffix -aris became English -ar, meaning 'relating to'.
items.cn: 指小形式 cellula「小房间」提供了形容词的词基；后缀 -aris 变成英语 -ar，表示「与……有关的」。

items.en: Robert Hooke described the small compartments of cork as cells in 1665, because they looked like the rooms of a monastery. The biological sense spread from that image.
items.cn: 1665 年，Robert Hooke 把软木中的小隔间称为 cell，因为它们看起来像修道院的小房间。生物学的义项就从这幅图像扩散开来。

items.en: As cell theory matured in the 19th century, cellular became the standard adjective for 'of cells'. The first uses are not precisely dated.
items.cn: 随着 19 世纪细胞学说成熟，cellular 成为表示「细胞的」的标准形容词。最早用例的年份并不精确。

items.en: Radio engineers in the 1940s and 1950s divided coverage into cells and called the system cellular; the telephone sense followed.
items.cn: 20 世纪 40 至 50 年代，无线电工程师把覆盖区分成一个个小区，称该系统为 cellular；电话义随后出现。

note.en: The first group separates words that look like cellular or share its root; the second separates 'of cells' from other levels and from the radio sense.
note.cn: 第一组区分看起来像 cellular 或共享词根的词；第二组把「细胞的」与其它层次以及无线电义分开。

entries.definition: The unit itself, or a small room or battery; cellular is the adjective that describes things made of or belonging to cells.
entries.definitionCN: 指单元本身，也可指小房间或电池；cellular 是描述「由细胞构成或属于细胞」的形容词。

entries.definition: A storage room below ground, from the same Latin cella but with a different vowel and meaning; it has nothing to do with biology.
entries.definitionCN: 指地下储藏室，与拉丁语 cella 同源，但元音与词义都不同，与生物学无关。

entries.definition: The fibrous substance in plant cell walls; it is named from cellula but is a noun for a material, not a general adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物细胞壁中的纤维物质，得名于 cellula，但是表示材料的可数名词，不是一般形容词。

entries.definition: In everyday British English, the ordinary word for a phone that moves with its user; cellular is the technical name of the network behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 在英式日常英语里指随身携带的电话；cellular 是支撑它的网络的技术名称。

entries.definition: Relating to life in general; cellular is narrower because it names one level of biological organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与生命有关；cellular 更窄，因为它只指生物组织的一个层次。

entries.definition: Full of holes that let fluid through; cellular describes a honeycomb pattern of compartments, which may or may not be open.
entries.definitionCN: 指布满可让流体通过的孔；cellular 描述蜂巢式的隔间格局，这些隔间未必相通。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cell + -ular: belonging to cells, as a small room belongs to a building.
normal.cn: cell + -ular：属于细胞的，就像小房间属于一栋楼。

normal.en: The family runs cell, cellularity, cellulose, cellulite and unicellular.
normal.cn: 同族词有 cell、cellularity、cellulose、cellulite、unicellular。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cellular structure, cellular network, cellular immunity, cellular phone.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细胞结构、蜂窝网络、细胞免疫、蜂窝电话。

normal.en: The honeycomb sense is the same image as cork under Hooke's microscope.
normal.cn: 蜂窝义与 Hooke 显微镜下软木的图像是同一幅图。

normal.en: The phone sense is technical history hiding inside an everyday word.
normal.cn: 手机义是一个日常词里藏着的技术史。

abstract.en: Think of a apartment block: each room is a cell, and the whole building is cellular.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋公寓楼：每个房间是一个细胞，整栋楼就是 cellular。

abstract.en: A cellular network is a honeycomb laid over a city, each hexagon a small listening post.
abstract.cn: 蜂窝网络就是铺在城市上的一张蜂巢，每个六边形都是一个小监听站。

abstract.en: A cellular automaton is a crowd where each person follows only the neighbours.
abstract.cn: 元胞自动机就像一群人，每个人只跟着邻居行动。

examples.en: Cellular structure differs sharply between plant and animal tissue.
examples.cn: 植物组织与动物组织的细胞结构差别很大。

examples.en: The company upgraded its cellular network in rural districts.
examples.cn: 该公司升级了农村地区的蜂窝网络。

examples.en: Cellular immunity depends on T cells rather than on antibodies alone.
examples.cn: 细胞免疫依赖 T 细胞，而不只是抗体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cell（小房间/细胞）+ -ular」→ 像小房间一样一格一格的 → 细胞的、蜂窝式的

root: 拉丁语 cella「小房间、储藏室」→ 指小形式 cellula「小房间」→ 形容词 cellula + -aris；英语 cellular。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses start from the small room inside the Latin word: cells as units, as a level of study, as a location, as a honeycomb network, a phone, an immune mode, a porous material, a computing grid, and at last a prison cell.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从拉丁词里那间「小房间」出发：细胞作为单元、作为研究层次、作为位置、作为蜂窝网络、作为电话、作为免疫方式、作为多孔材料、作为计算网格，最后回到牢房。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of small rooms side by side, each holding a complete living kit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排彼此相邻的小房间，每间都装着一套完整的生命装置。

branches.en: THE SMALL ROOM: the oldest image links biological cells and prison cells.
branches.cn: 小房间：最古老的意象把生物细胞与牢房连在一起。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGICAL LEVEL: the science of cells, and processes located inside them.
branches.cn: 生物学层次：研究细胞的科学，以及发生在细胞内部的过程。

branches.en: THE HONEYCOMB NETWORK: radio cells and the phone named after them.
branches.cn: 蜂窝网络：无线电小区以及因之得名的电话。

branches.en: CELL-BASED DEFENCE: immunity carried out by living cells.
branches.cn: 以细胞为主的防御：由活细胞执行的免疫。

branches.en: PATTERN AND RULE: porous materials and computing grids reuse the compartment image.
branches.cn: 格局与规则：多孔材料与计算网格重复使用「隔间」的意象。

intro.en: Cellular is a noun plus a Latin adjective ending: cell, from a diminutive of 'room', takes -ular.
intro.cn: cellular 是名词加拉丁形容词词尾：cell 来自「房间」的指小形式，再加 -ular。

latinIntro.en: Latin cella and its diminutive cellula underlie cell, cellar, cellular, cellulose and cellulite; -aris supplies the English ending -ar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cella 及其指小形式 cellula 支撑了 cell、cellar、cellular、cellulose、cellulite；-aris 提供英语词尾 -ar。

items.meaning: relating to cells; made of small compartments
items.meaningCN: 与细胞有关的；由小隔间构成的
items.example: The tissue has a cellular architecture.

items.meaning: the basic unit of life; a small room
items.meaningCN: 生命的基本单元；小房间
items.example: Every cell carries the same DNA.
items.exampleCN: 每个细胞都携带相同的 DNA。

items.example: The wine is kept in a cool cellar.
items.exampleCN: 葡萄酒存放在阴凉的地窖里。

items.meaning: the fibre of plant cell walls
items.exampleCN: 纸的主要成分是纤维素。

items.example: Multicellular life appeared late in Earth's history.
items.exampleCN: 多细胞生命在地球历史上出现较晚。

items.example: The parasite hides in an intracellular niche.
items.exampleCN: 这种寄生生物藏在细胞内的一个生态位里。
胶原蛋白构成一张细胞外网络。

definition_zh: 水泥；黏合剂；巩固；加强
definition_en: a grey powder that hardens when mixed with water and is used in building, or to join things firmly together
core_image: 灰色粉末遇水变硬，把两块石头粘成一体
scene: 建筑工地上尘土飞扬。Workers poured cement into the wooden frame.
sceneCN: 这里 cement 指「水泥」（第 1 个义项：遇水变硬的灰色建筑材料）；句意是工人把水泥倒进木模板里。

senses.title: A powder used in building
senses.definition: a grey powder made from lime and clay that hardens when mixed with water and sand
senses.definitionCN: 由石灰与黏土制成的灰色粉末，与水沙混合后变硬
senses.example: The wall is held together by cement.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙靠水泥黏合在一起。
senses.why: The Latin source meant rough broken stone, and the powder that binds such stones is the modern heir.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是粗糙的碎石，而把碎石黏住的粉末正是它的现代继承者。

senses.title: Something that binds people together
senses.definition: a shared feeling or interest that holds a group together
senses.definitionCN: 把一群人维系在一起的共同情感或利益
senses.example: Common work was the cement of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的工作是这支队伍的黏合剂。
senses.why: If cement holds stones, any force that holds people together can borrow the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然水泥能把石头黏住，任何把人维系在一起的力量都能借用这个词。

senses.title: To make something firm
senses.definition: to make a relationship, agreement or position stronger and harder to break
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、协议或地位更牢固、更难动摇
senses.example: The trip cemented their friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行巩固了他们的友谊。
senses.why: The verb applies the hardening of cement to any bond that becomes solid.
senses.whyCN: 动词把水泥变硬的过程用到任何变得牢固的纽带上。

intro.en: Cement goes back to a Latin word for rough cut stone, and only later named the powder that binds stones.
intro.cn: cement 可追到拉丁语中表示粗糙碎石块词，后来才指把石块黏住的粉末。

items.en: Caementum meant rough stone or rubble used in building.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caementum 指建筑用的粗石或碎石。

items.en: The noun comes from caedere, to cut, because the stone was cut into pieces.
items.cn: 该名词源自动词 caedere（切），因为石料是被切碎的。

items.en: Ciment named the binding material used with rubble in medieval walls.
items.cn: 古法语 ciment 指中世纪砌墙时与碎石同用的黏合材料。

items.en: English cement first means the mortar or binding powder itself.
items.cn: 英语 cement 最初就指灰浆或黏合粉本身。

items.en: Modern chemistry standardises the powder, and the verb extends to firm friendships and agreements.
items.cn: 现代化学使这种粉末标准化，动词义则扩展到牢固的友谊与协议。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the binding family, while the meaning group lists other building and joining materials.
note.cn: 形近组沿黏结词族展开，近义组列出其他建筑与黏合材料。

entries.definition: the process of binding particles together
entries.definitionCN: 把颗粒黏结在一起的过程

entries.definition: a machine that mixes cement with sand and water
entries.definitionCN: 把水泥与沙水混合的机器

entries.definition: a hard building material made of cement, sand and gravel
entries.definitionCN: 由水泥、沙和砾石制成的坚硬建材

entries.definition: a soft mixture used to join bricks
entries.definitionCN: 用来砌砖的软质混合物

entries.definition: a substance that sticks things together
entries.definitionCN: 把东西粘在一起的物质

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cut-stone root, the building compounds and the friendship phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用切石词根、建筑复合词以及友谊搭配。

normal.en: Cement comes from a Latin word for cut stone, because it began as rubble in a wall.
normal.cn: cement 来自拉丁语中表示切碎石料的词，因为它最初就是墙里的碎石。

normal.en: Cement, concrete and mortar are a stair: powder, then the mix, then the soft paste between bricks.
normal.cn: cement、concrete、mortar 像三级台阶：粉末、混合料、砖缝里的软浆。

normal.en: To cement a friendship is to let time harden the bond like setting cement.
normal.cn: cement a friendship 就是让时间像凝固的水泥一样把情谊变硬。

normal.en: Cement mixer keeps the word next to the machine that turns the powder into paste.
normal.cn: cement mixer 把词与那台把粉末变成浆的机器放在一起。

normal.en: The noun has no plural in ordinary use, so uncountable is the honest label.
normal.cn: 这个名词日常没有复数，所以标为不可数最诚实。

abstract.en: Picture grey powder sliding from a paper sack.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色粉末从纸袋里滑出来。

abstract.en: Picture a trowel smoothing wet grey paste over bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象泥刀把湿灰浆抹平在砖面上。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pressed together and held by something unseen.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手紧紧相握，被某种看不见的东西固定。

examples.en: The workers mixed cement and sand in a tub.
examples.cn: 工人把水泥和沙在盆里拌匀。

examples.en: A shared language cements the group.
examples.cn: 共同的语言把这个群体凝聚起来。

examples.en: The post is set in cement.
examples.cn: 这根柱子用水泥固定住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: cement 读音近似「塞门特」：把缝隙「塞」满，再「门」一关就黏牢了。

root: 源自拉丁语 caementum（粗石、碎石），出自 caedere（切），经古法语 ciment 进入英语，由石料转指黏合粉末。

sensesIntro.en: Cut stone becomes binding powder, the powder becomes a metaphor for human bonds, and the verb makes any bond harden.
sensesIntro.cn: 切碎的石料变成黏合粉末，粉末变成人际纽带的比喻，动词则让任何纽带变硬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey powder that hardens and locks two stones together.
core.cn: 核心意象：遇水变硬、把两块石头锁在一起的灰色粉末。

branches.en: The building powder keeps the physical sense closest to the Latin stone.
branches.cn: 建筑粉末义最接近拉丁语的石料本义。

branches.en: A shared interest binds people as cement binds stones.
branches.cn: 共同利益像水泥黏石头一样把人黏在一起。

branches.en: The verb hardens relationships the way cement hardens in air.
branches.cn: 动词让关系变硬，正如水泥在空气中凝固。

branches.en: Both depend on a material that sets and then cannot be moved.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖一种凝固后无法移动的材料。

branches.en: Both apply the builder's craft to human ties.
branches.cn: 两者都把建筑手艺用到人际纽带上。

intro.en: Cement forms abstract nouns with -ation and adjectives with -itious, plus the mixer compound.
intro.cn: cement 用 -ation 构成抽象名词、用 -itious 构成形容词，另有 mixer 复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin caementum and caedere are the stone and cut roots behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caementum 与 caedere 分别是这个词背后的石料与切割词根。

items.example: Cement sets hard in a day.

items.meaning: he or she strengthens a bond

items.example: The cement mixer roared all morning.
Caementum named rubble in Roman walls.
items.exampleCN: caementum 指罗马墙中的碎石。

latinEntries.example: Caementum is the source of cement.
latinEntries.exampleCN: caementum 是 cement 的来源。
caedere 解释了切石的画面。

definition_zh: n. 审查员；v. 审查并删改
definition_en: an official who checks books, films or news and removes what is not allowed; to remove such parts
core_image: 一支红笔划掉整段文字
scene: 审查员用红笔划掉了信里整整一段。The censor struck out a whole paragraph with a red pen.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：censor 指审查员；句意是审查员用红笔划掉信中一段。

senses.title: The official
senses.definition: an official who examines material and removes what is forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 检查材料并删去违禁内容的官员
senses.example: The censor demanded three cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 审查员要求删去三处。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin censor, a Roman official who assessed conduct.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语 censor，指古罗马评估品行的官员。

senses.title: To cut material
senses.definition: to examine and remove parts of a book, film or letter
senses.definitionCN: 检查并删去书、影片或信件中的部分
senses.example: The report was heavily censored.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告被大幅删改。
senses.why: The official duty became the act of cutting.
senses.whyCN: 官员的职责转化为删剪这一动作。

intro.en: Censor comes from Latin censor, a Roman official who assessed conduct, from censere, to judge.
intro.cn: censor 来自拉丁语 censor（评估品行的罗马官员），源自 censere（评判）。

items.en: Censere means to assess or judge.
items.cn: 拉丁语 censere 意为评估或评判。

items.en: A censor is a Roman assessing official.
items.cn: censor 是古罗马的评估官员。

items.en: Church censors check printed books.
items.cn: 十六世纪教会审查印刷书籍。

items.en: State censors watch the press.
items.cn: 十七世纪国家审查员监督报刊。

items.en: Film and radio face official censors.
items.cn: 二十世纪电影与广播面对官方审查。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cens- stem; the near-meaning group moves from scrutiny to suppression.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cens- 词干；近义组从细看延伸到压制。

normalIntro.en: A censor is a reader with a red pen and the power to stop.
normalIntro.cn: censor 是拿着红笔、有权叫停的读者。

normal.en: Censere means to judge.
normal.cn: censere 意为评判。

normal.en: Roman censors assessed conduct.
normal.cn: 古罗马监察官评估品行。

normal.en: Church censors checked books.
normal.cn: 教会审查员检查书籍。

normal.en: The verb means to cut passages.
normal.cn: 动词义为删去段落。

normal.en: The word grew into censorship.
normal.cn: 这个词发展出 censorship。

latinIntro.en: Centum, hundred, and gradus, step, are the two elements of the compound.

definition_zh: n. 蜈蚣；（尤指室内的）家蜈蚣
definition_en: a long thin crawling animal with many pairs of legs; also the common house species
core_image: 石头下面一条长身多足的虫子窜出来
scene: 一块石头下面钻出一条长腿的蜈蚣。A centipede slipped out from under a stone.

senses.title: The many-legged animal
senses.definition: a long thin animal with many segments and many pairs of legs, hunting at night

senses.example: A centipede ran across the kitchen floor.

senses.why: Latin centum is a hundred and pes is a foot, though the name overstates the count.

senses.title: The indoor species
senses.definition: the fast pale species that lives in damp houses and hunts other insects

senses.example: House centipedes hunt other insects at night.

senses.why: English applies the same name to the common indoor species.
senses.whyCN: 英语也用同一个名字称常见的室内种类。

intro.en: Centipede joins Latin centum, a hundred, and pes, a foot.

definition_zh: n. 集中化；中央集权化（英式拼写）
definition_en: the act of bringing power, control or activity under one centre; the British spelling
core_image: 所有箭头都从四面八方汇向一个点
scene: 政府把审批权收归一个部门，完成了彻底的集中化。The government moved all approvals into one department, a complete centralisation.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：centralisation 指集中化；句意是政府把审批权收归一个部门。

senses.title: Bringing things to one centre
senses.definition: the act of gathering control, records or services into a single place
senses.definitionCN: 把控制权、档案或服务集中到一处
senses.example: Centralisation of records cut waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 档案集中使等候时间缩短。
senses.why: The word is built from centre plus the suffix of process.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 centre 加上表示过程的词缀构成。

senses.title: Political central power
senses.definition: the transfer of political authority from regions to a national centre
senses.definitionCN: 把政治权威从地方转移到国家中心
senses.example: The reform deepened centralisation in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革加深了首都的中央集权。
senses.why: The political sense follows the general one of moving control inward.
senses.whyCN: 政治含义沿用把控制权向内收拢的一般含义。

intro.en: Centralisation builds on Latin centrum, a centre, through central and the verb centralise.
intro.cn: centralisation 经 central 与动词 centralise，建立在拉丁语 centrum（中心）之上。

definition_zh: 世纪；一百年；（板球）一百分
definition_en: a period of one hundred years, or a score of one hundred in cricket
core_image: 日历上整整一百年排成的一长条
scene: 钟楼每小时敲一次，记录着时间流逝。The tower has stood for a century.

senses.title: A hundred-year period
senses.definition: a period of one hundred years, often counted from a fixed starting point
senses.definitionCN: 一百年的时间，常从某个固定起点算起
senses.example: The bridge was built in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥建于上个世纪。

senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指一百名士兵组成的一队，后来同样的计数被用到年份上。

dict_mnemonic.text: cent 是一百：把一百年捆成一束，就是 century 世纪。

root: 源自拉丁语 centuria（百人队），出自 centum（一百），经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A hundred years is the everyday sense, while a hundred runs in cricket keeps the same count in sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 一百年是日常义项，板球中的一百分则在运动里保留同一个计数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hundred units gathered into a single block.
core.cn: 核心意象：一百个单位被捆成一大块。

branches.en: The time sense counts years in blocks of a hundred.
branches.cn: 时间义把年份按一百一组来数。

branches.en: The sporting sense counts points or runs in the same block.
branches.cn: 运动义按同样的一百来数分。

branches.en: Both keep the Latin count of one hundred.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留拉丁语「一百」的计数。

branches.en: Historical phrases such as turn of the century depend on the time sense.
branches.cn: 世纪之交一类历史短语依赖时间义。

branches.en: The plural centuries often means a very long stretch of time.
branches.cn: 复数 centuries 常指一段很长的时间。

intro.en: Century belongs to a large cent- family built on the Latin word for one hundred.
intro.cn: century 属于建立在拉丁语「一百」之上的庞大 cent- 词族。

latinIntro.en: Centum, one hundred, and centuria, a company of a hundred, are the two Latin sources.
latinIntro.cn: centum（一百）与 centuria（百人队）是两个拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: a period of one hundred years
items.exampleCN: 这发生在一个世纪以前。

items.example: The walls have lasted for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这些墙已经存续了几个世纪。

items.meaning: the leader of a hundred soldiers
items.exampleCN: 一名百人队长守着城门。
百年纪念音乐会座无虚席。
这位百岁老人仍每天散步。
他们办了一场百年晚宴。

items.meaning: a company of a hundred soldiers

latinEntries.exampleCN: centum 开启整个词族。

latinEntries.meaning: a company of a hundred men
latinEntries.exampleCN: centuria 是直接来源。

definition_zh: 陶瓷的；陶瓷制品；陶瓷材料
definition_en: made of fired clay or of a similar inorganic material; a ceramic object or material
core_image: 一只上釉的白瓷碗放在灯下，釉面反出冷光，旁边是一片未上釉的灰坯
scene: 工程师把一小片烧成的材料放进高温炉，测试它能否承受骤冷。The engineer placed a ceramic sample in the furnace to test how it survived sudden cooling.
sceneCN: 这里 ceramic 指「陶瓷材料」（第 3 个义项：经高温烧结的无机非金属材料）；句意为工程师把一片陶瓷样品放入炉中，测试它在骤冷后的状态。图中可辨识物件：高温炉、样品夹、温度表、冷却槽。

pos.zh: 陶瓷制品；陶瓷材料（常用复数指器物）

derivatives.zh: 陶瓷工艺；陶瓷学（加 -s 构成学科名）
以陶瓷方式；在陶瓷方面

senses.title: Made of fired clay
senses.definition: made of clay shaped and hardened by firing
senses.definitionCN: 由黏土塑形并经火烧硬制成的
senses.example: The floor was covered with ceramic tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 地面铺着瓷砖。
senses.why: ceramic is the adjective from the Greek word for potter's clay, so its first job is to describe clay ware.
senses.whyCN: ceramic 是来自希腊语「陶土」一词的形容词，因此首要用途是描述陶制器物。

senses.title: Relating to the ceramic arts
senses.definition: connected with the art and craft of making clay and porcelain objects
senses.definitionCN: 与制作陶器和瓷器的艺术手艺相关
senses.example: The gallery devotes one room to ceramic art.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊用一间展厅陈列陶瓷艺术。
senses.why: museums and studios use the adjective to mark the whole field rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与工作室用这个形容词标注整个领域，而不是单件器物。

senses.title: An engineered inorganic material
senses.definition: a hard, heat-resistant material made by firing inorganic powders, used in engineering
senses.definitionCN: 由无机粉末烧结而成、坚硬耐热的材料，用于工程
senses.example: A ceramic coating protects the turbine blade from heat.
senses.exampleCN: 一层陶瓷涂层保护涡轮叶片免受高温。
senses.why: materials science widened the word from pots to any fired inorganic solid with useful hardness.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学把这个词从陶罐扩展到任何烧成的、具备可用硬度的无机固体。

senses.title: A ceramic object, usually in the plural
senses.definition: an object made of fired clay or porcelain, often spoken of in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用陶土或瓷土烧成的物件，常以复数形式出现
senses.example: Each ceramic is tested for porosity before packing.
senses.exampleCN: 每件陶瓷制品在包装前都要检测孔隙率。
senses.why: the countable noun turns the material name into one manufactured item.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词用法把材料名转化为一件制成品。

senses.title: Building ware such as tiles and sanitary fittings
senses.definition: fired clay products used in construction, such as tiles, sinks and toilets
senses.definitionCN: 用于建筑的烧制黏土产品，如瓷砖、水槽与便器
senses.example: The bathroom uses ceramic fittings throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室全部使用陶瓷洁具。
senses.why: construction speaks of ceramic rather than pottery because the products are industrial, not artisanal.
senses.whyCN: 建筑行业说「陶瓷」而不说「陶器」，因为这些产品是工业品，不是手工艺品。

senses.title: Material used in dentistry and medicine
senses.definition: a fired inorganic material used for crowns, implants and medical devices
senses.definitionCN: 用于牙冠、植入体与医疗器械的烧制无机材料
senses.example: The crown is made of a translucent ceramic that matches the tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗牙冠用一种与牙齿颜色相近的半透明陶瓷制成。
senses.why: dentistry needed materials that are hard, inert and tooth-coloured, and ceramic supplied all three.
senses.whyCN: 牙科需要坚硬、惰性且颜色接近牙齿的材料，陶瓷正好三者兼具。

senses.title: The glazed surface of such ware
senses.definition: the glassy fired coating on clay ware, considered as a finish
senses.definitionCN: 陶器表面烧成的玻璃质涂层，作为一种饰面
senses.example: A blue ceramic glaze ran down the side of the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 一层蓝色釉顺着碗壁流下。
senses.why: the adjective came to describe the glaze itself, since the finish is what the eye actually sees.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也用来描述釉本身，因为肉眼真正看到的就是这层饰面。

senses.title: Hard plates used in armour
senses.definition: a hard ceramic plate used in protective armour to stop projectiles
senses.definitionCN: 用于防护装甲、阻挡弹丸的硬质陶瓷板
senses.example: The vest carries a ceramic plate over the chest.
senses.exampleCN: 这件防弹背心在胸前装有一块陶瓷板。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrowed again in armour design, where extreme hardness matters more than heat resistance.
senses.whyCN: 工程义在装甲设计中再次收窄，那里极致的硬度比耐热更重要。

intro.en: Ceramic comes from Greek keramikos 'of pottery', from keramos 'potter's clay, pottery', and entered English through learned Latin and French forms in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceramic 来自希腊 keramikos「陶器的」，源于 keramos「陶土、陶器」，十九世纪经学术拉丁语与法语形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Keramos named potter's clay and pottery. Its earlier origin is not established; a link to kerannynai 'to mix' is a hypothesis, and a pre-Greek source is also proposed.
items.cn: keramos 指陶土与陶器。其更早来源没有定论；把它联系到 kerannynai「混合」只是假说，也有人提出源自前希腊语。

items.en: Keramikos meant 'of pottery' and was used of the potters' quarter and of clay ware generally.
items.cn: keramikos 意为「陶器的」，用于指陶工区，也泛指陶制器物。

items.en: Learned Latin took the Greek adjective as ceramicus and the noun as ceramica, keeping the Greek root intact.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语把这个希腊形容词写作 ceramicus，名词写作 ceramica，希腊词根原样保留。

items.en: English adopted ceramic in the nineteenth century as the scientific and artistic term for fired clay ware.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪采用 ceramic，作为烧制陶器的科学与艺术术语。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was extended to engineering ceramics, dental ceramics and armour plates.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词扩展到工程陶瓷、牙科陶瓷与装甲板。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of keramos is unsettled, so any older form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：keramos 的前希腊语历史没有定论，为它提出的更早形态均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes with different roots or endings; group two holds the ware names that are often used as if they were synonyms of ceramic.
note.cn: 第一组是词根或词尾不同却形近的词；第二组是常被当作 ceramic 同义词使用的器物名。

entries.definition: The plural noun for the art and science of ceramic ware, or for the objects themselves; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指陶瓷艺术与科学的复数名词，也指器物本身；它不是形容词。

entries.definition: A maker or student of ceramics; the ending marks a person, not a material.
entries.definitionCN: 陶瓷艺人或研究者；词尾标出的是人，不是材料。

entries.definition: The protein of hair, horn and nails, from Greek keras 'horn'; it looks close but has no connection with clay.
entries.definitionCN: 毛发、角与指甲中的蛋白质，来自希腊 keras「角」；形近，但与黏土毫无关系。

entries.definition: A second spelling of the person noun, built with -icist rather than -ist; both are current.
entries.definitionCN: 指人名词的另一种拼法，用 -icist 而非 -ist；两种写法都在使用。

entries.definition: The everyday mass noun for fired clay ware and the craft that makes it; ceramic is its technical and industrial counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指烧制陶器及其手艺的日常名词；ceramic 是它的技术与工业对应词。

entries.definition: Porous clay ware fired at a lower temperature, usually glazed to hold water.
entries.definitionCN: 较低温度烧成的多孔陶器，通常上釉以防渗水。

entries.definition: Dense, non-porous clay ware fired high enough to be waterproof without glaze.
entries.definitionCN: 烧成温度较高、致密不渗水的陶器，无须上釉即可防水。

entries.definition: The finest ceramic ware, white and translucent, fired at very high temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 最精细的陶瓷，白色半透明，烧成温度极高。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real industrial phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构词成分、真实工业短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek keramos 'potter's clay' plus -ic 'relating to': relating to clay ware.
normal.cn: 希腊 keramos「陶土」加 -ic「与……相关」：与陶制器物相关。

normal.en: The family runs ceramic, ceramics, ceramist, ceramicist, ceramically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ceramic、ceramics、ceramist、ceramicist、ceramically。

normal.en: Industry phrases mark the technical sense: advanced ceramic, ceramic coating, ceramic matrix.
normal.cn: 工业短语标出技术义：先进陶瓷、陶瓷涂层、陶瓷基体。

normal.en: Building suppliers speak of ceramic tiles and ceramic fittings, never of pottery tiles.
normal.cn: 建材商说瓷砖与陶瓷洁具，从不说「陶器砖」。

normal.en: Dentistry pairs the word with crown and implant: ceramic crown, ceramic implant.
normal.cn: 牙科把这个词与牙冠、植入体搭配：陶瓷冠、陶瓷植入体。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl so hard that it rings like a bell but shatters like glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗硬得敲起来像钟，却又能像玻璃一样碎裂。

abstract.en: Picture a heat shield that began as a lump of grey powder.
abstract.cn: 想象一块隔热罩，最初只是一团灰色粉末。

abstract.en: Picture a tooth rebuilt from the same stuff as a teacup.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗牙齿用与茶杯相同的材料重建。

examples.en: The façade is clad in ceramic panels that resist graffiti.
examples.cn: 外立面覆以抗涂鸦的陶瓷板。

examples.en: Ceramic bearings run smoothly without oil.
examples.cn: 陶瓷轴承无需润滑油即可平稳运转。

examples.en: The museum bought a set of ceramic vessels from the site.
examples.cn: 博物馆从该遗址购得一套陶瓷器皿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cera（蜡似的光）+ mic」——釉面像蜡一样发亮的东西 → 陶瓷

root: 希腊 keramos「陶土、陶器」→ keramikos「陶器的」→ 学术拉丁 ceramicus → 英语 ceramic。keramos 的更早来源不确定，与前希腊语或 kerannynai「混合」的联系均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from the potter's clay outward: the clay ware itself, the art, the engineered material, one object, building fittings, dental work, the glaze, and finally armour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从陶土向外扩散：陶制器物本身、陶瓷艺术、工程材料、单件制品、建筑洁具、牙科修复、釉面，最后是装甲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft clay passing through fire and coming out hard, glossy and useful.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软的黏土穿过火焰，出来时坚硬、光亮而有用。

branches.en: WARE: the adjective describes fired clay objects, and the countable noun names one of them.
branches.cn: 器物：形容词描述烧制的陶制品，可数名词则指其中一件。

branches.en: SURFACE AND ART: what the eye meets is the glaze, and the craft that produces it is ceramic art.
branches.cn: 表面与艺术：眼睛看到的是釉，制作釉面的手艺就是陶瓷艺术。

branches.en: ENGINEERING HARDNESS: the same material serves turbine blades and armour plates where hardness is the point.
branches.cn: 工程硬度：同一种材料用于涡轮叶片与装甲板，那里关键就是硬度。

branches.en: BUILDING: tiles and sanitary fittings carry the word into construction as an industrial category.
branches.cn: 建筑：瓷砖与洁具把这个词作为工业类别带入建筑业。

branches.en: BODY: dentistry borrows the material because it is hard, inert and close in colour to enamel.
branches.cn: 身体：牙科借用这种材料，因为它坚硬、惰性且颜色接近牙釉质。

intro.en: Ceramic is a Greek root with a Greek adjective ending, routed through learned Latin and then into English.
intro.cn: ceramic 是希腊词根加希腊形容词词尾，经学术拉丁语转入英语。

latinIntro.en: Learned Latin kept the Greek forms as ceramicus and ceramica; English drew ceramic from them and later added -s to make the field name.
latinIntro.cn: 学术拉丁语保留希腊形式写作 ceramicus 与 ceramica；英语由此取得 ceramic，后来又加 -s 构成学科名。

items.example: The root names the material before the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先命名材料，再命名器物。

items.example: The suffix turns the material into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把材料变成形容词。

items.meaning: relating to fired clay; made of it
items.example: A ceramic liner protects the pipe.

items.meaning: the field, or a set of objects
items.example: The ending makes ceramics a subject name.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使 ceramics 成为学科名。

items.meaning: the art and science of ceramic ware
items.example: Ceramics is taught in the engineering faculty.

items.meaning: a maker or student of ceramics
items.example: The ceramist tested three new glazes.
items.exampleCN: 这位陶艺家试了三种新釉。

items.example: The ceramicist works mainly in porcelain.
items.exampleCN: 这位陶艺家主要用瓷土创作。

items.meaning: a glassy fired coating on clay ware
items.example: A ceramic glaze sealed the porous body.
items.exampleCN: 一层陶瓷釉封住了多孔的坯体。

latinEntries.structure: ceramica, ceramicae (f., first declension, Latinized Greek)

definition_zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐
definition_en: a grass grown for its edible grain, the grain itself, or a breakfast food made from such grain
core_image: 早餐桌上的一碗燕麦片，旁边放着麦穗与一袋面粉，三样东西都来自同一种草
scene: 厨房台面上摆着一碗泡了牛奶的燕麦片，旁边是一束干麦穗和一袋面粉。Cereal crops cover more land than any other food group.
sceneCN: 这里指「谷类作物」（第 1 个义项：作为作物类别）；句意为谷类作物占用的土地超过任何其他食物类别。

pos.zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐

derivatives.zh: cereal + grain（组合成分）→ 谷物籽粒（语义偏移：从作物类别缩小到籽粒本身）
cereal + crop（组合成分）→ 谷类作物（语义偏移：强调田间栽培对象）
cereal + bar（组合成分）→ 谷物棒（语义偏移：转为便携食品）
breakfast（早餐）+ cereal → 谷物早餐（语义偏移：专指早餐碗里的加工谷物）
cereal + box（组合成分）→ 谷物包装盒
cereal + bowl（组合成分）→ 谷物碗

senses.title: A grass grown for grain
senses.titleCN: 为收籽粒而种植的禾草
senses.definition: any grass cultivated mainly for its edible starchy grain, such as wheat, rice or maize
senses.definitionCN: 主要为可食淀粉籽粒而栽培的任何禾草，如小麦、稻或玉米
senses.example: Wheat is the cereal best suited to this cold plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦是最适合这块寒冷高原的谷类作物。
senses.why: The word names the plant category, and the botanical link is that all of them are grasses.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名植物类别，其植物学联系在于它们都是禾草。

senses.title: Cereal grain as a mass
senses.definition: the grain of such plants considered as a food or trade commodity
senses.definitionCN: 这类植物的籽粒，作为食品或贸易商品来看
senses.example: Cereal is shipped in bulk from the lake port.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物从这个湖港以散装方式运出。
senses.why: The plant and its product are named by one word because the grain is the reason the plant is grown.
senses.whyCN: 植物与产物用同一个词命名，因为籽粒正是种植它的理由。

senses.title: A breakfast food from grain
senses.definition: a processed breakfast food made from toasted or flaked cereal grains, countable in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 由烘烤或压片的谷物制成的加工早餐食品，英式用法可数
senses.example: The shelf holds six kinds of cereal.
senses.exampleCN: 货架上摆着六种谷物早餐。
senses.why: In the twentieth century the product took the name of its raw material, and British usage made it countable.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪时产品沿用了原料之名，英式用法又使它可数。

senses.title: A bowl of cereal
senses.definition: a serving of breakfast cereal, usually with milk
senses.definitionCN: 一份谷物早餐，通常加牛奶
senses.example: He eats a bowl of cereal standing up.
senses.exampleCN: 他站着吃一碗谷物早餐。
senses.why: A mass noun can be counted through its container, so a bowl becomes the unit of everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词可以借容器计数，于是「一碗」成为日常使用的单位。

senses.title: Grain used as animal feed
senses.definition: cereal grain fed to livestock rather than milled for people
senses.definitionCN: 喂给家畜、而非磨给人吃的谷类籽粒
senses.example: Most of the cereal goes to feed, not to flour.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分谷物用作饲料，而非磨成面粉。
senses.why: The same harvest splits by end use, and feed is the largest destination in many regions.
senses.whyCN: 同一批收成按最终用途分流，在许多地区饲料是最大去向。

senses.title: Adjectival: made from grain
senses.definition: describing a product, field or policy connected with cereal grain
senses.definitionCN: 描述与谷物有关的产品、田地或政策
senses.example: Cereal production rose after the irrigation canal opened.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉渠开通后谷物产量上升。
senses.why: The noun attributively modifies another noun, a common English way of making a category adjective.
senses.whyCN: 名词作定语修饰另一名词，是英语构成类别形容词的常见方式。

senses.title: A crop in a rotation
senses.definition: a cereal crop considered as one stage in a field rotation
senses.definitionCN: 作为田间轮作一个环节的谷类作物
senses.example: The rotation puts cereal after legumes.
senses.exampleCN: 轮作把谷物安排在豆类之后。
senses.why: Agronomy treats the plant as a slot in a sequence, which gives the word a planning sense.
senses.whyCN: 农学把这种植物当作序列中的一格，于是这个词有了规划义。

senses.title: Grain as a traded commodity
senses.definition: cereal grain priced and traded on markets, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在市场上定价与交易的谷类籽粒，常用复数
senses.example: Cereal prices fell after a record harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 创纪录的收成之后，谷物价格下跌。
senses.why: Trade abstracts the plant into a contract, and the market sense is the most abstract of the eight.
senses.whyCN: 贸易把植物抽象成合约，市场义是八义中最抽象的一层。

intro.en: Cereal comes from Latin cerealis, of Ceres, the Roman goddess of grain, through French céréale. The breakfast sense is a twentieth-century development. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cereal 来自拉丁 cerealis「刻瑞斯的」，刻瑞斯是罗马谷物女神，经法语 céréale 进入英语。早餐义是二十世纪的发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ceres was the Roman goddess of grain and harvest, and her name stands at the head of the whole family.
items.cn: 刻瑞斯是罗马的谷物与丰收女神，她的名字位于整个词族的顶端。

items.en: Cerealis meant of Ceres or of grain, and the neuter plural cerealia named her festival and the grain offered at it.
items.cn: cerealis 意为刻瑞斯的或谷物的；中性复数 cerealia 指她的节庆与节上献的谷物。

items.en: French céréale carried the adjective and noun into English in the nineteenth century as a botanical and agricultural term.
items.cn: 法语 céréale 在十九世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语，作为植物学与农学术语。

items.en: English cereal first named the grain plants, then their grain, and only later the processed breakfast product.
items.cn: 英语 cereal 先指谷类植物，再指其籽粒，最后才指加工后的早餐产品。

items.en: The breakfast food sense grew in the early twentieth century with commercial flaked and puffed cereals, and British usage made it countable.
items.cn: 早餐食品义在二十世纪初随商业化的压片与膨化谷物而发展，英式用法又使其可数。

items.en: Source uncertain (goddess's deeper name): the pre-Latin origin of Ceres is reconstructed and debated, so any Indo-European root offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（女神名的更深词源）：Ceres 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构且有争议，凡为其给出的印欧词根均属假说。

note.en: Group one holds words that sound like cereal or name its source; group two holds words for grain and grain foods.
note.cn: 第一组是读音像 cereal 或指其来源的词；第二组是表示谷物及谷物食品的词。

entries.definition: A story or set arranged in a series, from Latin series; it sounds identical to cereal but shares no origin.
entries.definitionCN: 按序列编排的故事或一组事物，来自拉丁 series；与 cereal 读音相同，但无共同来源。

entries.definition: The Roman goddess of grain whose name gives cereal; the word is a proper noun, not a food.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马谷物女神，其名给出 cereal；这是专有名词，不是食物。

entries.definition: The seed of a cereal plant; cereal alone can name the plant, the grain or the breakfast food.
entries.definitionCN: 谷类植物的籽粒；单说 cereal 可指植物、谷物或早餐食品。

entries.definition: The seed or the harvested mass; cereal is the plant category or the breakfast product.
entries.definitionCN: 种子或收获后的总量；cereal 是植物类别或早餐产品。

entries.definition: In British English it means the chief local cereal, often wheat; in American English it means maize. Cereal avoids that split.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语指当地主要谷物，常为小麦；美式英语指玉米。cereal 可避开这一分歧。

entries.definition: A sweetened mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten as a breakfast cereal; it is one product, not the category.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦、坚果与果干加糖混合的早餐谷物食品；它是单一产品，不是类别。

entries.definition: A hot dish of grain boiled in water or milk; cereal is the raw material or the cold packaged product.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物加水或牛奶煮成的热食；cereal 是原料或冷食包装产品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ceres, the grain goddess, stands behind the word.
normal.cn: 谷物女神刻瑞斯站在这个词的背后。

normal.en: The family runs cereal, cereal grain, cereal crop, breakfast cereal, cereal bar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cereal、cereal grain、cereal crop、breakfast cereal、cereal bar。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: cereal crops in the field, breakfast cereal in the bowl.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：田里的谷类作物，碗里的谷物早餐。

normal.en: The homophone serial belongs to a different family and means a series.
normal.cn: 同音词 serial 属于另一词族，意为系列。

normal.en: British corn and American corn part company, which is why cereal is the safer category word.
normal.cn: 英式 corn 与美式 corn 分道扬镳，因此 cereal 是更安全的类别词。

abstract.en: Picture a goddess holding one sheaf that becomes a bowl, a bag of flour and a box on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女神手持一束麦穗，它变成一只碗、一袋面粉与货架上的一盒产品。

abstract.en: Picture a field that is also a price chart, each row of stalks a line on the market page.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田同时是一张价格图，每一行麦秆都是行情页上的一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a breakfast table where every object can be traced back to one kind of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张早餐桌，每样东西都能追到同一种草。

examples.en: Cereal crops need nitrogen at the start of the season.
examples.cn: 谷类作物在生长季开始时需要氮。

examples.en: She poured the milk over her cereal.
examples.cn: 她把牛奶倒在谷物早餐上。

examples.en: Cereal prices are sensitive to weather in exporting regions.
examples.cn: 谷物价格对出口地区的天气很敏感。

dict_mnemonic.text: Ceres（谷物女神）+ -al（……的）→ 女神的谷物 → 谷类作物、谷物，再到碗里的谷物早餐；与同音的 serial（系列）无关。

root: 拉丁 Ceres（罗马谷物女神，属格 Cereris）+ -alis「……的」→ cerealis「谷物的」→ 法语 céréale → 英语 cereal；Ceres 的更深词源属重构且有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grass: the plant, its grain, the milled product, the bowl, the feed, the adjective, the rotation slot and the market contract.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种草展开：植物、籽粒、加工产品、碗中之物、饲料、形容词、轮作位置与市场合约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind of grass can become a sheaf, a sack of grain, a bag of flour and a bowl on a breakfast table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种草可以变成一束麦穗、一袋谷粒、一袋面粉和早餐桌上的一只碗。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the botanical category comes first.
branches.cn: 植物：植物学类别最先出现。

branches.en: THE MASS AND THE MARKET: grain as a bulk food and as a priced contract.
branches.cn: 总量与市场：谷物既是散装食品，也是定价合约。

branches.en: THE BOWL: the processed product and the serving it fills.
branches.cn: 碗：加工产品以及它装满的一份。

branches.en: THE FEED TROUGH: the same harvest diverted to animals.
branches.cn: 饲料槽：同一批收成转向动物。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY LABEL: adjective use and the crop's place in a rotation.
branches.cn: 类别标签：形容词用法与作物在轮作中的位置。

intro.en: Cereal is a Latin adjective turned noun, built from a divine name and a suffix, so its morphology runs through the goddess rather than through a verb.
intro.cn: cereal 是由拉丁形容词转成的名词，由一个神名与后缀构成，因此其构词沿女神名展开，而非沿动词展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin Ceres, genitive Cereris, supplies the stem, and -alis makes the relational adjective cerealis; the neuter plural cerealia named the goddess's festival.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Ceres（属格 Cereris）提供词干，-alis 构成关系形容词 cerealis；中性复数 cerealia 指女神的节庆。

items.structure: Ceres, Cereris (Latin proper noun, third declension)
items.example: Ceres gave her name to the whole category.
items.exampleCN: 刻瑞斯把名字给了整个类别。

items.example: The suffix builds cerealis from the goddess's name.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由女神名构成 cerealis。

items.example: The adjective described both the goddess and the crop.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时描述女神与作物。

items.meaning: a grain plant or its food
items.example: Cereal entered English as a learned term.
items.exampleCN: cereal 作为学术用语进入英语。

items.meaning: the seed of a cereal plant
items.example: The cereal grain is milled into flour.

items.meaning: a cereal grown in a field
items.example: The cereal crop rotated with beans.

items.meaningCN: 加工过的早餐谷物食品
items.example: Breakfast cereal replaced porridge in many homes.
items.exampleCN: 在许多家庭里，谷物早餐取代了粥。

items.example: The cereal bar fits in a coat pocket.
items.exampleCN: 谷物棒能塞进外套口袋。

items.meaning: the packaging of a breakfast cereal
items.example: The cereal box carries the nutrition table.

definition_zh: 典礼；仪式；礼节；客套
definition_en: a formal set of actions on an important occasion, or formal polite behaviour
core_image: 一群人按固定次序完成一整套动作
scene: 婚礼上宾客按顺序站好，等待交换誓言。The wedding ceremony lasted an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 ceremony 指「典礼」（第 1 个义项：重要场合的正式仪式）；句意是婚礼仪式持续了一个小时。

senses.title: A formal event
senses.definition: a formal set of actions performed on an important public or religious occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在重要公共或宗教场合进行的一整套正式动作
senses.example: The graduation ceremony begins at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业典礼九点开始。
senses.why: The Latin source named a sacred rite, and the word still keeps that sense of a fixed set of actions.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指宗教仪式，这个词仍保留整套固定动作的含义。

senses.title: Formal polite behaviour
senses.definition: the formal behaviour expected on polite occasions, sometimes seen as unnecessary
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌场合所要求的正式举止，有时被视为多余
senses.example: They greeted us without ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不拘礼节地跟我们打了招呼。
senses.why: Once a rite sets the proper forms of address, following those forms becomes a kind of ceremony in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 仪式一旦规定了得体的称呼方式，遵守这些形式在日常生活中也就成了一种客套。

intro.en: Ceremony comes from the Latin word for a sacred rite, and English first used it for religious observance.
intro.cn: ceremony 源自拉丁语中表示宗教仪式的词，英语最初用它指宗教礼拜。

items.en: Caerimonia named a religious rite and the awe that went with it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caerimonia 指宗教仪式以及伴随的敬畏。

items.en: The adjective caeremonialis described what belonged to such rites.
items.cn: 形容词 caeremonialis 描述与这类仪式相关的事物。

items.en: Old French ceremonie carried the word into court and church usage.
items.cn: 古法语 ceremonie 把该词带入宫廷与教会用语。

items.en: English ceremony first means a religious observance or a formal rite.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语 ceremony 先指宗教礼拜或正式仪式。

items.en: The word widens to weddings, openings and the polite forms called ceremony.
items.cn: 词义扩展到婚礼、开幕式以及被称为客套的礼节。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the ceremony family, while the meaning group lists rites and formal occasions.
note.cn: 形近组沿 ceremony 词族展开，近义组列出仪式与正式场合的说法。

entries.definition: very formal and correct in behaviour
a set of actions always done the same way
entries.definitionCN: 总按同样方式完成的一套动作

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the fixed order of a rite to weddings, openings and polite distance.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把仪式的固定次序与婚礼、开幕式以及礼貌的距离联系起来。

normal.en: A ceremony is a set order of actions: everyone knows where to stand and what to say.
normal.cn: ceremony 是固定次序的动作：谁站哪里、说什么都有定规。

normal.en: Wedding ceremony and opening ceremony both mark a moment people want to remember.
normal.cn: wedding ceremony 与 opening ceremony 都标记人们想记住的时刻。

normal.en: Without ceremony means doing something plainly, with no polite fuss.
normal.cn: without ceremony 意为不带客套、直截了当地做事。

normal.en: To stand on ceremony is to insist on polite forms and distance.
normal.cn: stand on ceremony 就是坚持礼数与距离。

normal.en: Ceremonial is the adjective for the event, ceremonious for a stiff person.
normal.cn: ceremonial 形容仪式本身，ceremonious 形容拘谨的人。

abstract.en: Picture a line of people moving in step through a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人踩着同一节拍穿过大厅。

abstract.en: Picture a stage with ribbons, speeches and a fixed order of turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一个有彩带、致辞和固定顺序的舞台。

abstract.en: Picture two people bowing slightly instead of shaking hands.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人微微鞠躬而不是握手。

examples.en: The award ceremony was held in the main hall.
examples.cn: 颁奖典礼在大厅举行。

examples.en: She left the room without ceremony.
examples.cn: 她不拘礼节地离开了房间。

examples.en: The old ceremony is performed every spring.
examples.cn: 这项古老的仪式每年春天举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: cere 联想到「因此」：因为重要，所以要按固定次序走完一整套动作，这就是仪式。

root: 源自拉丁语 caerimonia（宗教仪式、敬畏），经古法语 ceremonie 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The sacred rite gives the event sense, and the required forms of behaviour give the politeness sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 宗教仪式给出活动义，被要求的行为形式则给出礼节义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed sequence of actions performed in public.
core.cn: 核心意象：在众人面前按固定次序完成的一套动作。

branches.en: The event sense keeps the full public performance.
branches.cn: 活动义保留完整的公开仪式。

branches.en: The politeness sense shrinks the rite into manners.
branches.cn: 礼节义把仪式缩减为举止。

branches.en: Both rest on actions that follow a set order.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在按固定次序进行的动作上。

branches.en: Weddings, openings and graduations supply the modern occasions.
branches.cn: 婚礼、开幕式与毕业典礼提供现代场合。

branches.en: Phrases such as without ceremony reject the polite forms.
branches.cn: without ceremony 一类短语否定这些礼貌形式。

intro.en: Ceremony extends into ceremonial and ceremonious, two adjectives with different shades.
intro.cn: ceremony 扩展出 ceremonial 与 ceremonious 两个含义有别的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Caerimonia and caeremonialis are the Latin noun and adjective behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: caerimonia 与 caeremonialis 是英语词族背后的拉丁语名词与形容词。

items.exampleCN: 她那郑重的鞠躬显得冷淡。

items.example: A judge officiated at the wedding.

latinEntries.exampleCN: caerimonia 以 ceremonie 进入法语。
caeremonialis 变成 ceremonial。

definition_zh: 当然；肯定地；无疑
definition_en: without any doubt, or used to agree politely to a request
core_image: 一句话被钉死，没有半点摇晃的余地
scene: 他点头答应，语气里没有一丝犹豫。She will certainly help us.
sceneCN: 这里 certainly 指「肯定地」（第 1 个义项：毫无疑问地）；句意是她肯定会帮我们。

senses.title: Without any doubt
senses.definition: in a way that leaves no doubt about what is said
senses.definitionCN: 以对所说不留疑问的方式
senses.example: The plan will certainly succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划肯定会成功。
senses.why: The adverb simply adds -ly to certain, so it carries the same settled sureness into the action.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是在 certain 后加 -ly，把同样的确定感带给动作。

senses.title: A polite yes
senses.definition: used in speech to agree strongly and politely to a request
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于爽快而有礼地同意请求
senses.example: Certainly, please come in.
senses.exampleCN: 当然，请进。
senses.why: A speaker who is completely sure can answer with the adverb alone, and that firm answer hardened into a polite formula.
senses.whyCN: 完全有把握的人可以只用一个副词作答，这种干脆的回答便固化成了礼貌套语。

intro.en: Certainly is the adverb of certain, built on the Latin adjective for something settled.
intro.cn: certainly 是 certain 的副词，建立在表示「已定」的拉丁语形容词之上。

items.en: Certus meant decided and free from doubt.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为已决断、无可怀疑。

items.en: The adverb certa mente grew from the same stem in later Latin.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中，副词 certa mente 由同一词干发展而来。

items.en: Old French certain supplied the adjective to English.
items.cn: 古法语 certain 把形容词提供给英语。

items.en: English adds -ly and forms certainly as a firm statement.
items.cn: 英语加上 -ly，构成表示坚定陈述的 certainly。

items.en: The word also becomes a polite yes in everyday conversation.
items.cn: 这个词在日常对话中也成了礼貌的「当然」。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cert- family, while the meaning group lists adverbs of strong agreement.
note.cn: 形近组沿 cert- 词族展开，近义组列出表示强烈肯定的副词。

entries.definition: in a way no one can doubt

normalIntro.en: These hooks pair the -ly ending with the cert- family and the polite yes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 -ly 词尾与 cert- 词族以及礼貌的「当然」配在一起。

normal.en: Certain plus -ly gives certainly: the adjective becomes the way an action is done.
normal.cn: certain 加 -ly 得 certainly：形容词变成动作进行的方式。

normal.en: Certainly not and most certainly sit at the two ends of agreement.
normal.cn: certainly not 与 most certainly 站在同意程度的两端。

normal.en: Almost certainly leaves a small crack of doubt, but certainly alone leaves none.
normal.cn: almost certainly 留一道小小的怀疑缝隙，单用 certainly 则一点不留。

normal.en: Answering Certainly at the door is the polite version of yes.
normal.cn: 在门口答一句 certainly，就是礼貌版的「好」。

normal.en: Uncertain plus -ly would be uncertainly, the opposite ending in doubt.
normal.cn: uncertain 加 -ly 是 uncertainly，方向相反，落在怀疑上。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed down hard on a document.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章被重重按在文件上。

abstract.en: Picture a head nodding once, firmly, with no hesitation.
abstract.cn: 想象一次干脆的点头，毫无迟疑。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line drawn without a single wobble.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画得笔直、毫不抖动的线。

examples.en: She is certainly the best player here.
examples.cn: 她无疑是这里最好的选手。

examples.en: Certainly, I can send you the file today.
examples.cn: 当然，我今天就能把文件发给你。

examples.en: The weather will almost certainly improve tomorrow.
examples.cn: 明天天气几乎肯定会好转。

dict_mnemonic.text: certain 加 -ly 就是「以确定的方式」：说出口时，仿佛在句子上盖了个章。

root: 由 certain 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，certain 源自拉丁语 certus（已定的）。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb states sureness first, and spoken use turns that sureness into a polite yes.
sensesIntro.cn: 副词先表达确定，口语用法又把这份确定变成礼貌的应允。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a statement sealed so it cannot wobble.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话被牢牢封住，不会晃动。

branches.en: The first sense states firm sureness.
branches.cn: 第一个义项表达坚定的确定。

branches.en: The second sense uses that sureness as agreement.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这份确定用作应允。

branches.en: Both come from the same cert- stem of settled things.
branches.cn: 两者都来自表示「已定」的同一 cert- 词干。

branches.en: Almost certainly softens the claim without reversing it.
branches.cn: almost certainly 只减弱而不反转这个断言。

branches.en: Certainly at the door signals welcome and consent.
branches.cn: 在门口说 certainly，表示欢迎与同意。

intro.en: Certainly belongs to the cert- group, where -ly marks the adverb and -ty the noun.
intro.cn: certainly 属于 cert- 组，其中 -ly 标记副词，-ty 标记名词。

latinIntro.en: Certus and cernere, the settled and the deciding, underlie the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: certus（已定的）与 cernere（判定）支撑着整组词。

items.example: We need certainty before we move.
items.exampleCN: 行动前我们需要确定性。
cernere 是 certus 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: certus 产生 certain。
cernere 是更深的词根。

definition_zh: 证书；证明书；凭证
definition_en: an official document that proves a fact, a qualification or an achievement
core_image: 一张盖了章、写满事实的纸
scene: 考试通过后，她拿到一张盖着红章的纸。The school gave her a certificate.
sceneCN: 这里 certificate 指「证书」（第 1 个义项：证明资格或成就的正式文件）；句意是学校发给她一张证书。

senses.title: A document of qualification
senses.definition: an official paper showing that a person has completed a course or gained a skill
senses.definitionCN: 表明某人完成课程或获得技能的正式文件
senses.example: She has a teaching certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一张教师资格证书。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to make certain, and a certificate is the paper that makes a fact certain to others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「使确定」，而证书就是把某件事向他人确定下来的那张纸。

senses.title: Written proof of a fact
senses.definition: a document that records a fact such as a birth, a marriage or an ownership
senses.definitionCN: 记录出生、婚姻或所有权等事实的文件
senses.example: Bring your birth certificate to the office.
senses.exampleCN: 把出生证明带到办公室。
senses.why: Births and marriages are facts that must be proved to strangers, so the same paper that makes them certain records them.
senses.whyCN: 出生与婚姻都是必须向陌生人证明的事实，于是同一张使事实确定的纸也承担了记录功能。

intro.en: Certificate joins the Latin words for sure and to make, so it names a paper that makes a matter sure.
intro.cn: certificate 把拉丁语中「确定」与「做」两个词合在一起，指使事情确定下来的纸。

items.en: Certus meant settled, and facere meant to make or do.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为已定，facere 意为制作或做。

items.en: Certificare meant to make something certain in writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certificare 意为以书面方式使某事确定。

items.en: Medieval French certificat named the written document itself.
items.cn: 中古法语 certificat 直接指这份书面文件。

items.en: English certificate first names an official written statement.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 certificate 先指正式的书面陈述。

items.en: The word covers birth certificates, school certificates and certificates of origin.
items.cn: 这个词涵盖出生证明、学业证书与原产地证书。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cert- family of official proof, while the meaning group lists other papers and awards.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示官方证明的 cert- 词族展开，近义组列出其他文件与奖项。

entries.definition: to state officially that something is true
an official permission to do something
a paper given on completing a course
entries.definitionCN: 完成课程后获得的文书

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into make plus certain and attach it to the papers people keep.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词拆成「使」加「确定」，并把它挂到人们保存的那些纸上。

normal.en: Cert plus ficare: make certain. A certificate is a paper that makes a fact certain.
normal.cn: cert 加 ficare，意为使确定；certificate 就是让事实确定下来的纸。

normal.en: Birth certificate, marriage certificate and certificate of origin are three common papers.
normal.cn: 出生证明、结婚证书与原产地证书是三种常见文件。

normal.en: To issue a certificate is to hand over official proof.
normal.cn: issue a certificate 就是交出官方证明。

normal.en: Certify is the verb, certification the act, and certificate the paper.
normal.cn: certify 是动词，certification 是行为，certificate 是那张纸。

normal.en: A certificate course ends with a paper rather than a degree.
normal.cn: certificate course 以一张证书而非学位收尾。

abstract.en: Picture a red stamp landing on a clean sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚红章落在一张干净的白纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a frame on a wall holding one precious sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一个相框里只装着一张珍贵的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a desk drawer where every important paper is kept.
abstract.cn: 想象一个抽屉，专门存放每一张重要文件。

examples.en: You need a medical certificate to join the course.
examples.cn: 参加这门课程需要一份体检证明。

examples.en: The certificate was signed by the head teacher.
examples.cn: 这张证书由校长签署。

examples.en: Keep your certificates in a safe place.
examples.cn: 把证书放在安全的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: cert 是「确定」，fic 是「做」：把确定的事做在纸上，就是证书。

root: 源自拉丁语 certificare（使确定），由 certus（已定的）与 facere（做）复合，经中古法语 certificat 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One sense covers proof of skill, and the other covers proof of a recorded fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项覆盖技能证明，另一个义项覆盖被记录事实的证明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper that turns a claim into an official fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张把说法变成官方事实的纸。

branches.en: The qualification sense proves a completed course or skill.
branches.cn: 资格义证明完成的课程或技能。

branches.en: The fact sense records birth, marriage or ownership.
branches.cn: 事实义记录出生、婚姻或所有权。

branches.en: Both make a claim certain through official writing.
branches.cn: 两者都通过官方书写使某种说法确定。

branches.en: Certificate courses build towards this first sense.
branches.cn: 证书课程朝着第一个义项积累。

branches.en: Birth and marriage certificates are the plainest examples of the second.
branches.cn: 出生与结婚证书是第二个义项最直白的例子。

intro.en: Certificate shares its stem with certify and certification, and -ficare marks the making.
intro.cn: certificate 与 certify、certification 同干，-ficare 标记「使…」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Certus, sure, and facere, to make, combine in certificare.
latinIntro.cn: certus（确定的）与 facere（做）在 certificare 中结合。

items.example: Show your certificate at the gate.

latinEntries.exampleCN: certificare 变成 certify。
certus 是词根形容词。

definition_zh: v. 证明；正式确认；发证书给；给…发执照
definition_en: to state officially that something is true or of a required standard; to give someone a licence
core_image: 医生在病历上签下名字并盖章
scene: 医生签字证明这份病历属实。The doctor signed to certify that the record was true.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：certify 指证明；句意是医生签字证明病历属实。

senses.title: To confirm as true
senses.definition: to state officially in writing that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 以书面方式正式声明某事属实
senses.example: The officer certified the signature.
senses.exampleCN: 官员证明了签名的真实性。
senses.why: Latin certus means sure and facere means to make.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 certus 意为确定，facere 意为使。

senses.title: To license someone
senses.definition: to give a person official permission to work in a trade
senses.definitionCN: 正式准许某人从事某种职业
senses.example: The board certified her as a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认证她为护士。
senses.why: The licence sense grows from confirming a standard.
senses.whyCN: 执照含义由确认标准引申而来。

intro.en: Certify joins Latin certus, sure, and facere, to make.
intro.cn: certify 结合拉丁语 certus（确定的）与 facere（使成为）。

items.en: Certus and facere give the sense of making sure.
items.cn: certus 与 facere 带来「使确定」的含义。

items.en: The verb enters law as to confirm in writing.
items.cn: 十四世纪进入法律，意为书面确认。

items.en: Officials certify signatures and accounts.
items.cn: 十六世纪官员证明签名与账目。

items.en: Guilds certify the skills of members.
items.cn: 十八世纪行会认证会员技艺。

items.en: Bodies certify products and standards.
items.cn: 二十世纪机构认证产品与标准。

items.en: Certify covers both proof and licensing.
items.cn: 现代兼指证明与发证。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cert- stem; the near-meaning group names other ways of confirming.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cert- 词干；近义组列出其他确认方式。

entries.definition: To state that something is true.

normalIntro.en: Make certain with a signature.
normalIntro.cn: 用一个签名把事确定下来。

normal.en: Certus means sure.
normal.cn: certus 意为确定。

normal.en: Facere means to make.
normal.cn: facere 意为使。

normal.en: Certify means to make sure.
normal.cn: certify 意为使确定。

normal.en: A signature does the making.
normal.cn: 签名完成这个「使」。

normal.en: A licence is proof of standard.
normal.cn: 执照就是标准的证明。

abstract.en: Certainty stamped onto paper.
abstract.cn: 把确定盖在纸上。

abstract.en: Trust with a date and a seal.
abstract.cn: 带着日期与印章的信任。

abstract.en: A promise someone will stand behind.
abstract.cn: 有人愿意作保的承诺。

examples.en: Two witnesses must certify the will.
examples.cn: 必须有两名证人证明遗嘱。

examples.en: The lab certified the water as safe.
examples.cn: 实验室证明水质安全。

examples.en: She was certified to teach chemistry.
examples.cn: 她获得了教化学的资格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色体法爱」——色体之法，爱盖章作证。

root: 拉丁语 certus（确定的）+ facere（使）→ certificare → 英语 certify

sensesIntro.en: To certify is first to make certain, then to hand over the paper that proves it.
sensesIntro.cn: certify 先使确定，再交付证明它的纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature and seal turning a claim into proof
core.cn: 核心意象：签名与印章把说法变成证据

branches.en: A pen resting on a dotted line.
branches.cn: 停在虚线上的笔。

branches.en: A stamp pressed onto a copy.
branches.cn: 盖在副本上的印章。

branches.en: A framed licence on a clinic wall.
branches.cn: 诊所墙上的执照。

branches.en: A board voting on a candidate.
branches.cn: 委员会对候选人表决。

branches.en: Certainty given a public form.
branches.cn: 被赋予公开形式的确定。

intro.en: Certify carries a root of certainty; the list below adds words of truth, trust and proof.
intro.cn: certify 含有「确定」词根；下面列出真实、信任与证明词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin certus is sure, facere is to make and fides is trust.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为确定，facere 意为使，fides 意为信任。

latinEntries.exampleCN: certus 产生 certain 与 certify。
facere 产生 fact 与 certify。
fides 产生 faith 与 fidelity。

definition_zh: adj. 颈部的；子宫颈的
definition_en: relating to the neck, or to the cervix of the uterus
core_image: 低头太久后按住后颈的那只手
scene: 他在桌前坐了一整天，颈部一阵酸痛。A whole day at the desk left his cervical spine stiff.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cervical 指颈部的；句意是一整天伏案让他的颈椎发僵。

senses.title: Of the neck
senses.definition: relating to the neck, especially its vertebrae
senses.definitionCN: 与颈部有关的，尤指颈椎
senses.example: Hours at the screen strained his cervical muscles.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间看屏幕使他的颈部肌肉紧张。
senses.why: Latin cervix first meant the neck of the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cervix 最初指身体的颈部。

senses.title: Of the cervix
senses.definition: relating to the cervix, the lower part of the uterus
senses.definitionCN: 与子宫颈（子宫下部）有关的
senses.example: Cervical screening is offered every three years.
senses.exampleCN: 宫颈筛查每三年提供一次。
senses.why: Anatomy extended the neck word to the neck of the womb.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把「颈」这个词延伸到子宫的颈部。

intro.en: Cervical comes from Latin cervix, the neck, a word also used for the neck of the womb.
intro.cn: cervical 来自拉丁语 cervix（颈），该词也用于指子宫颈。

items.en: Cervix means the neck of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cervix 指身体的颈。

items.en: The adjective names the neck vertebrae.
items.cn: 十六世纪该形容词指颈部椎骨。

items.en: Cervix is applied to the neck of the womb.
items.cn: 十七世纪 cervix 用于指子宫颈。

items.en: Cervical enters clinical descriptions.
items.cn: 十九世纪进入临床描述。

items.en: Cervical screening becomes routine.
items.cn: 二十世纪宫颈筛查成为常规。

items.en: Cervical covers neck and womb alike.
items.cn: 现代兼指颈部与子宫颈。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cerv- stem; the near-meaning group names other regions of the body.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cerv- 词干；近义组列出身体其他部位。

entries.definition: The neck, or the neck of the womb.

normalIntro.en: Cervix is the neck, so cervical means of the neck.
normalIntro.cn: cervix 是颈，cervical 就是颈部的。

normal.en: Cervix means a neck.
normal.cn: cervix 意为颈。

normal.en: The adjective adds -al.
normal.cn: 形容词加 -al。

normal.en: Cervical spine sits in the neck.
normal.cn: 颈椎位于颈部。

normal.en: The womb has a neck too.
normal.cn: 子宫也有一个「颈」。

normal.en: So one word covers both.
normal.cn: 于是同一个词兼指两处。

abstract.en: The narrow doorway of the body.
abstract.cn: 身体狭窄的门道。

abstract.en: A hinge held upright all day.
abstract.cn: 整天竖着的铰链。

abstract.en: Where the trunk narrows into the head.
abstract.cn: 躯干收窄通向头部之处。

examples.en: She has a cervical injury from the fall.
examples.cn: 她因跌倒造成颈部受伤。

examples.en: The cervical vertebrae support the head.
examples.cn: 颈椎支撑着头部。

examples.en: Cervical screening detects early changes.
examples.cn: 宫颈筛查能发现早期变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色未扣」——脖子上的扣子色未扣好，露出颈部。

root: 拉丁语 cervix（颈）→ cervicalis → 英语 cervical

sensesIntro.en: One Latin word for neck serves both the spine and the womb.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁语里「颈」这个词同时服务于脊椎与子宫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow neck joining a heavy body to its top
core.cn: 核心意象：连接沉重躯体与其顶端的细颈

branches.en: A hand pressed to the back of the neck.
branches.cn: 按在后颈上的手。

branches.en: A chair with no head support.
branches.cn: 没有头托的椅子。

branches.en: A clinic appointment card.
branches.cn: 诊所的预约卡。

branches.en: A slide under a microscope.
branches.cn: 显微镜下的涂片。

branches.en: A narrow passage in two parts of the body.
branches.cn: 身体两处共有的狭窄通道。

intro.en: Cervical is built on a Latin word for neck; the list below adds words of body regions and procedures.
intro.cn: cervical 建于拉丁语「颈」之上；下面列出身体部位与医疗操作词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cervix is a neck, vertebra a joint of the spine and uterus the womb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cervix 意为颈，vertebra 意为脊椎关节，uterus 意为子宫。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cervix 产生 cervical 与 cervix。
vertebra 产生 vertebral 与 vertebrate。
uterus 产生 uterine 与 uterus。
